items.headline: Ten men, one goal — City win a wild Manchester derby
items.body: The 199th Manchester derby had everything. Phil Foden got sent off early for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, leaving City a man down for over an hour at Old Trafford — but they hung on and won it anyway, Erling Haaland heading home a back-post cross that survived a nervy VAR offside check for a 1-0 win. United, stuck near the bottom, couldn't make the extra man count.
items.say: The Manchester derby yesterday was chaos — City had a guy sent off in the first half, played the rest a man down, and still won 1-0 on a Haaland goal that barely survived the video review. United fans are furious.

items.headline: So close for the home crowd — Zverev denies Shelton in the final
items.body: The American drought rolls on. Top seed Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 in the US Open final to grab his second Grand Slam title, leaving U.S. men still without a major since Andy Roddick in 2003. Shelton, the first American man in the final in over 20 years, gave New York a run but couldn't get over the line.
items.say: Shelton so nearly did it at the US Open — first American guy in the final in 20-plus years — but Zverev beat him in four sets. That American men's major drought is now going on 23 years.

items.headline: Golden again — Team USA rallies past France for a 5th straight World Cup
items.body: Down 14 in the second half, the U.S. women flipped the switch. They outscored France 30-12 in the third quarter and cruised to a 97-79 win in Berlin for their fifth consecutive FIBA World Cup title. Breanna Stewart (22 points, 10 boards) was named tournament MVP for the second time, with Jackie Young turning in a stat line no one had ever posted in a World Cup final.
items.say: Team USA women just won their fifth World Cup in a row — but they had to rally from 14 down against France to do it. Breanna Stewart was the MVP. That program basically never loses.

links.text: ESPN — how USA rallied for gold

items.headline: A points explosion — Bears drop 59, Packers get stunned
items.body: Football's really back. The Bears and Panthers combined for 96 points in a 59-37 shootout, the highest-scoring Week 1 game ever, with Caleb Williams accounting for four touchdowns and Chicago's backs running for six scores. Elsewhere the Vikings shocked the Packers 39-22 after backup Carson Wentz came off the bench, and the Cardinals upset the Chargers.
items.say: The NFL's back and Week 1 was bonkers — the Bears won a 59-37 track meet, the highest-scoring opener ever. Ninety-six points in one game. You riding with a team this year?

items.headline: Chaos beyond Texas — Oklahoma State stuns No. 6 Oregon
items.body: Texas over Ohio State wasn't even the only shocker. Oklahoma State — which hadn't beaten an FBS team in nearly two years — walked into a top-6 Oregon and won 39-31, ending a 21-game skid behind quarterback Drew Mestemaker's 317 passing and 109 rushing yards. Michigan knocked off Oklahoma too, and unranked South Florida stunned No. 13 Florida. The polls got a total reshuffle.
items.say: Saturday was pure chaos in college football — besides Texas beating Ohio State, Oklahoma State went into Oregon and won as huge underdogs after not beating anybody good in two years. The whole top 25 got scrambled.

items.headline: Reacher goes full throttle — 'Runner' hits theaters
items.body: If you like your action loud and a little goofy, this one's for you: 'Runner' opened Friday with Alan Ritchson (yes, Reacher himself) as an ex-soldier racing a life-saving medical delivery across town while a cartel hunts him — with Owen Wilson as his very unlikely partner. It's Angel Studios' first R-rated movie, and it cracked the box-office top five out of the gate.
items.say: There's a new action movie out called 'Runner' — it's the Reacher guy, Alan Ritchson, paired up with Owen Wilson of all people, doing a beat-the-clock cartel chase. Sounds like a fun dumb Friday-night watch.

items.headline: Six years later — Jhené Aiko is back with 'Westside Whimsy'
items.body: R&B fans have been waiting. Jhené Aiko surprise-dropped 'Westside Whimsy' — her first album since 2020's 'Chilombo' — a breezy 20-track love letter to '90s California, cruising and the coast. The headliner everyone's clicking on: 'So Good,' a smooth link-up with Kendrick Lamar that's already near the top of YouTube's trending chart.
items.say: New Jhené Aiko album finally landed — her first in six years — and there's a song on it with Kendrick Lamar that everyone's talking about. Real easy, laid-back California vibe. What's been on your rotation lately?

items.headline: Regular folks, real backstabbing — 'The Traitors: New Blood' starts Thursday
items.body: The sneakiest game on TV comes to network: 'The Traitors: New Blood' premieres Thursday on NBC with a two-hour opener, and this time it's an all-civilian cast — no reality stars — playing Alan Cumming's castle game of secret murderers, banishments and a prize pot up to $250,000. Same Scottish Highlands, same gloriously dramatic host, brand-new set of everyday backstabbers.
items.say: The Traitors is back Thursday, but this version's all regular people instead of reality stars — just normal folks lying to each other in a Scottish castle. It's the most fun 'who do you trust' show on TV. You watch that one?
